title: Smooth surjective parameter scheme of maximal tori
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $G$ a reductive $S$-group scheme in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. For an $S$-scheme $U$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal T_G(U)$ be the set of closed subgroup schemes $T\hookrightarrow G\times_S U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product] such that $T$ is a $U$-torus and $T_{\bar u}$ is a maximal torus of $G_{\bar u}$ for every geometric point $\bar u\to U$. Here a $U$-torus is a relative torus in the sense of [def-sfb-relative-torus], that is, a group scheme which on an fppf covering is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^{r_i}$ for finite ranks $r_i\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(V)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)^\times$ and fppf coverings are [def-pc-fppf-site]. A geometric point is a morphism from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field; maximal means maximal for inclusion among tori over that field. Pullback of subgroup schemes makes $\mathcal T_G$ a contravariant functor on $S$-schemes. There is an $S$-scheme $Q$ with a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(U,Q)\simeq\mathcal T_G(U)$ for every $U$. Its structural morphism $Q\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. No Noetherian or connectedness hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.6 and Corollary 3.2.7, printed pp.94-95; reductive specialization of the smooth surjective scheme of maximal tori, before choosing etale-local sections. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative reductive-group structural theorem.

proof.text: First verify the fppf sheaf condition for $\mathcal T_G$. For compatible closed torus subgroups over a covering of $U$, their quasi-coherent ideal sheaves in $G_U$ have the canonical overlap identifications. Convert the covering to an fpqc covering and apply quasi-coherent module descent, including its full faithfulness, to the ideals and their inclusions into $\mathcal O_{G_U}$. The descended submodule is an ideal: its multiplication into $\mathcal O_{G_U}/\mathcal I$ is zero because its pullback is zero and descent is faithful. The cited ideal-to-closed-subscheme construction gives $T\hookrightarrow G_U$ with exactly these pullbacks. Multiplication, inverse and unit restrict to $T$: their composites into the quotient ideal vanish on the covering, hence vanish by the same faithful descent. Their group identities and uniqueness are tested on the covering. The relative-torus condition holds because the covering followed by the given splitting coverings is still an fppf covering. For any geometric point of $U$, base change of the covering is surjective, so a geometric point above it tests the same geometric-maximality condition. If its fibre at the original geometric point lay in a strictly larger torus, the inclusion would remain strict after that faithfully flat field extension, contradicting maximality upstairs. Thus $T$ is geometrically maximal. This proves existence and uniqueness of gluing, without assuming $U$ affine or Noetherian.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.6 proof, first sentence (fppf sheaf); ideal descent is Stacks descent.tex Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent).

proof.text: For each $s\in S$, choose a split maximal torus of $G_{\bar s}$ using the existence assertion of the Borel-pair node. Apply the geometric-torus lifting node to obtain a split torus in $G$ over an affine flat locally finitely presented neighborhood $S'\to S$ of $s$. The torus is maximal at the marked point. Apply the split-torus maximality-openness clause and restrict to an affine open neighborhood of that point; call it $V_s$. Then the split torus $T_s\subseteq G_{V_s}$ is geometrically maximal everywhere on $V_s$. These maps are flat and locally finitely presented, and their images cover $S$, since each contains the chosen $s$; they therefore form an fppf covering. Use the finite-affine-refinement clause for fppf coverings on the affine scheme $S$ to obtain finitely many affine $V_i\to S$ covering $S$, each with a split geometrically maximal torus $T_i$. Let $V=\coprod_iV_i$. This is a singleton fpqc cover: it is flat componentwise, and the finitely many affine open summands cover its image $S$, as required by the definition of fpqc covering. The ranks of the $T_i$ need not agree.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.6 proof, first paragraph; use Proposition 3.1.9 and its fppf lifting argument, before choosing a maximal torus globally.

proof.text: Fix $i$. Apply the normalizer-quotient node to $G_{V_i}$ and its split torus $T_i$, obtaining $X_i=G_{V_i}/N(T_i)$ smooth and quasi-affine over $V_i$. Its structure map is surjective: for every point of $V_i$, the identity section of $G_{V_i}$ followed by $G_{V_i}\to X_i$ supplies a point over it. For any $V_i$-scheme $W$, conjugation sends $g\in G(W)$ to the closed maximal torus $g(T_i)_Wg^{-1}$. This is unchanged on a right coset of $N(T_i)(W)$. Step 1 therefore extends this map to the fppf coset sheaf represented by $X_i$. It is injective: locally lift two sections to $g,h$; equality of their subgroup functors is equivalent to $h^{-1}g\in N(T_i)$ by the defining normalizer formula, hence to equality of their right cosets. Equality of the sections then follows from the sheaf condition. Local lifting to cosets and local detection of equality use the cited set-valued sheafification-sections theorem. This constructs a natural injection $\operatorname{Hom}_{V_i}(W,X_i)\hookrightarrow\mathcal T_G(W)$.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.6 proof, second paragraph: quotient by the normalizer and the stabilizer calculation.

proof.text: Given any $T'\in\mathcal T_G(W)$, apply the fppf conjugacy node to $(T_i)_W$ and $T'$ in $G_W$. Both are closed relative tori and geometrically maximal on every fibre. There is an fppf covering $W_a\to W$ and $g_a\in G(W_a)$ with $g_a(T_i)_{W_a}g_a^{-1}=T'_{W_a}$. On an overlap, $g_b^{-1}g_a$ belongs to the normalizer because both conjugates equal the same subgroup $T'$. The right cosets therefore agree and glue to a section of $X_i$ over $W$, using that representable functors are fpqc sheaves and fppf coverings are fpqc. Its image is $T'$ by step 1, and it is unique by step 3. Pulling back the local $g_a$ pulls back this coset section, so the bijection is natural for every $W\to V_i$. No global conjugating element is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.6 proof, second paragraph and the entire two-maximal-tori argument on printed p.95.

proof.text: Put $X'=\coprod_iX_i$ over $V=\coprod_iV_i$ using scheme coproducts. It is quasi-affine over $V$ by quasi-affineness on the affine open cover $\{V_i\}$ of the target. Steps 3-4 identify its functor over $V$ with $\mathcal T_G$ restricted to $V$ (sections over a scheme over $V$ are specified on its disjoint open-and-closed inverse images of the summands). On $V\times_SV$, the two pullbacks of $X'$ consequently represent the same functor. Full faithfulness of Yoneda gives the unique comparison isomorphism that preserves the torus section. On $V\times_SV\times_SV$, both composites preserve that same section, so faithfulness gives the cocycle. Apply effective fpqc descent for quasi-affine schemes to the singleton covering $V\to S$, giving an $S$-scheme $Q$ with $Q\times_SV\simeq X'$ and this specified datum. For any $S$-scheme $U$, maps $U\to Q$ are the compatible local maps on $U\times_SV$ by representable fpqc descent. Their local torus sections are compatible by the defining comparison, and step 1 identifies them with precisely $\mathcal T_G(U)$. This gives the required natural bijection for all $U$.

source.place: Theorem 3.2.6 proof, opening descent reduction; Stacks descent.tex Tag 0247 (lemma-quasi-affine).

proof.text: Each restriction $X_i\to V_i$ of $X'\to V$ is smooth, so $X'\to V$ is smooth by the local definition. The singleton fpqc covering $V\to S$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact (it is a finite disjoint union of morphisms between affine schemes). Apply smooth fpqc base descent to $Q\to S$ and obtain smoothness. Finally, for $s\in S$, choose $v\in V$ above it. The corresponding $X_i\to V_i$ is surjective by step 3, hence some $x\in X'$ lies above $v$. Its image in $Q$ lies above $s$. Thus $Q\to S$ is surjective as well.

tool_uses.why: Use fppf coverings for fpqc module and scheme descent and obtain a finite affine refinement.
Descend quasi-coherent ideals and their inclusions; the unit has no separate ideal-descent equivalence.
Turn the descended ideal into the actual closed subgroup scheme.
Identify local subgroup ideals with flat pullbacks of the descended ideal.
Pull the covering back to a geometric point to test maximality.
Base change the covering to arbitrary test schemes in the functor-of-points argument.
Glue quotient sections and identify maps into the descended scheme.
Combine finitely many local charts and their quotients into one covering and one descent datum.
Obtain local right-coset representatives of quotient sections; set-valued sheafification is essential here.
Check the disjoint-union quotient is quasi-affine over its disjoint-union base.
Produce the unique torus-preserving scheme isomorphisms on overlaps and their cocycle.
Effectively descend the local quotient scheme along the fpqc cover; this is the generic scheme-descent tool used by Conrad.
Descend smoothness of the assembled quotient scheme.
Check quasi-compactness of the finite affine covering used for smoothness descent.
Check quasi-compactness of affine covering members.

Composing fppf coverings is elementary. Step 2 checks the hypotheses of the Borel-pair node (split maximal torus), torus-fppf-lift (smooth affine fp G, kappa(s') inside Omega) and the second clause of fibre-openness (fibres connected, so G0=G). The finite affine refinement comes from the 022C clause, so V is affine and V->S is fpqc. Step 3: gN maps to gTg^-1 on right cosets, and injectivity is checked against the node's normalizer formula. Step 4 (conjugacy) gives local conjugators that glue by 023Q. Step 5: 01SM gives quasi-affineness, Yoneda gives the canonical descent datum and its cocycle, 0247 gives effectivity, and representable descent gives Hom(U,Q)=T_G(U). Step 6: 02VL applies (V->S is flat, quasi-compact, surjective); surjectivity comes from the identity section. New node split-torus-normalizer-quasi-affine-quotient is Conrad 2.3.1 specialised to a split torus, with Rem 2.3.5 for smoothness of G->X; tested on r=0, G=T and diagonal T in SL2; not a duplicate of relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer (which gives no quotient).
